text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- Parliament approved at the first reading the licence agreement between Latvia and oil companies Amoco and Olje Prospektering. The second and the final reading of the agreement is scheduled for October 24.
- The foreign ministry has issued a statement which says that by concluding an agreement with AMOCO/OPAB Latvia is not establishing unilaterally its maritime border with Lithuania.
- The prime ministers of Latvia and Lithuania are meeting in Palanga (Lithuania) to continue talks on the maritime border.
- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs is on an official visit to Estonia. He met with Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi and Foreign Minister Siim Kallas.
- Russia informed the U.K. about its intention to submit to the U.N. General Assembly a draft resolution about the situation in the sphere of human rights in Latvia and Estonia.
DIENA

- Shkele and the prosecutor's office said that the prosecutor will investigate an incident when a police car knocked down a boy in the centre of Riga and then fled the scene. So far the police have refused to name the official who was driving.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- Most experts at the international conference-exhibition 'Banks and Finance in the Baltics'96' agreed that Estonia is the Baltics leader in providing favourable environment for investments.
- Former minister of finance, Aivars Kreituss, will work on the parliament's budget and finance committee.
BIZNES & BALTIYA
- The foreign ministry is to stop issuing visas at most of Latvia's border crossings from November 20.
- The economics ministry has decided that before being privatised the state-owned energy company Latvenergo will be transformed into a holding company.
SM
- Parliament voted against giving non-citizens the right to vote in the local elections.
DIENAS BIZNESS

- The agriculture ministry and the Institute of Agroeconomics are elaborating a System of Market and Price Information to provide Latvian agricultural producers with information on prices in different regions of Latvia.

- Minister of Economics, Guntars Krasts, says there is a need for a general free trade area law in Latvia. The lack of such a law has delayed the elaboration of the bill on establishing a free trade zone in Liepaja.
